# Agent Configuration

> Env var reference for the platform: the agent runtime (`runtime/`) and the
> admin service (`admin/`). Related: [agent-runtime.md](agent-runtime.md),
> [admin-service.md](admin-service.md), [agent-ops.md](agent-ops.md),
> [agent-api.md](agent-api.md), [chat-service.md](chat-service.md).

---

## Agent Config

All options are env vars; there is no file-based fallback for agent config. Secrets must be supplied as env vars and are never stored in config files. Coding-extension settings (task store, PR reconciler passes, loop orchestrator, review/patch policy) are documented with the coding extension in the [shipwright repo](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/configuration-agent.md).

### Per-agent fields

Unlike the env vars below, these fields live on the Agent database record, not the environment. They are set via the admin API (`POST`/`PATCH /agents/:id`) or the admin UI. See [agent-api.md](agent-api.md#agents) for the request/response contract.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repos` | `string[]` | `[]` | `org/repo` strings this agent is scoped to. Seeded from the Specialty manifest at creation, editable via `PATCH /agents/:id` or the admin UI. Repos added here are auto-cloned into `<workspace>/repos/` on the next config sync (~60s) by `runtime/sync-config-clone.ts` (`syncClonedRepos`); a failed clone is retried on the next tick. |
| `restrictSlackToMembers` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, only users listed in this agent's `AgentMember` rows can message the agent on Slack. When `false`, all Slack users can. Settable at creation and editable via `PATCH /agents/:id` or the admin UI. Enabling it with no members configured returns a non-blocking warning. |
| `cleanupMergedWorktrees` | `boolean` | `true` | Runtime-owned policy field, synced live every ~60s into `runtime/cleanup-merged-worktrees-ref.ts`; defaults to `true` until the first sync. |
| `cleanupAfterDays` | `integer` | `14` | Runtime-owned policy field, synced live into `runtime/cleanup-after-days-ref.ts` (default `14` until the first sync). `runtime/worktree-reaper.ts` reads it to force-remove `worktrees/<repo>-<branch>` directories older than this many days. |
| `trialExpiresAt` | `DateTime` | `null` | Trial expiry timestamp. Nullable; can be set, updated or cleared via `PATCH /agents/:id`. When it passes into the past, the admin service's `TrialExpirySweeper` (see `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`) disables every enabled AgentCronJob for that agent, and `runtime/slack.ts`'s `isTrialExpired()` gate blocks all inbound Slack messages with a "trial ended" notice. |
| `accountId` | `string \| null` | `null` | Owning account. Platform admins set or clear it via `PATCH /agents/:id` (403 for non-admin session members; 404 for an unknown account) or the Assign/Unassign controls on `/admin/accounts/:id`. For in-cluster agents the admin service then reconciles that one agent's workload so the tenant pod label and CPU limit follow the change (skipped for self-hosted agents; a reconcile failure is returned as a `warning`). Historical rows owned by other services are not moved to the new account. |
| `podServiceAccountName` | `string \| null` | `null` | Pod ServiceAccount name (COS-48.1). Nullable; settable by platform admins only via `PATCH /agents/{id}` (409 when the flag is off, 422 for agents with a per-agent federated identity; see [agent-api.md](agent-api.md)). Only rendered into provisioned pods when `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ENABLED` is `enabled`; ignored otherwise. Cannot coexist with Anthropic federation for the same agent. |
| `trialExpiryWarnedAt` | `DateTime` | `null` | Trial expiry warning timestamp. Written internally by the trial-expiry warning sweeper when it sends its alert. Read-only via the API (not settable via `PATCH`); included in `GET`/`PATCH` responses for display. |

### Claude / Anthropic

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `string` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Claude model used for each agent invocation. Seeded into a new agent's env at creation (admin `createAgent`) so it is visible and editable in the agent's env view; defaults live in `lib/default-agent-env.ts`. Secrets (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`) are never defaulted. |
| `ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_MODEL` | `string` | — | Fallback model if the primary is unavailable. |
| `ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVEL` | `string` | — | Effort/thinking level passed to Claude (e.g. `extended`, `auto`, `none`). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `3600000` | Hard **ceiling** timeout in milliseconds for a single `claude -p` session spawned by the runtime (`runtime/claude.ts`). A backstop, not the primary timeout (see `SHIPWRIGHT_CLAUDE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`). When total elapsed time exceeds it, the process is killed and a `ClaudeTimeoutError` (`reason: "ceiling"`) is raised, even if stdout stayed active. Defaults to 1 hr (`DEFAULT_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MS` in `lib/claude-timeout.ts`); a non-positive-integer value falls back to the default. Lives in the agent's own env; set per agent through the admin service's `POST`/`PATCH /agents/:id/envs`. `ClaudeTimeoutError` and `ClaudeRunError` carry a `sessionId` captured from the leading `system`/`init` stream-json line when one arrived before the failure, so a failed run can still be resumed on the next attempt. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CLAUDE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `1500000` | Idle-reset timeout in milliseconds for a single `claude -p` session (`runtime/claude.ts`), the **primary** timeout in practice. Restarted on every stdout line; fires (kills the process, raises `ClaudeTimeoutError` with `reason: "idle"`) only when the session goes silent for this long. Defaults to 25 min. Falls back to the default when unset or not a positive integer. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `string` | — | Anthropic API key. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Claude Code OAuth token (alternative to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Env-var-only (secret). |

**Run telemetry is not OpenTelemetry.** Per-run measurements (first-turn context baseline, turns, tool calls, per-skill attribution, context fingerprint) are captured from the Claude CLI stream and stored on `AgentCronRun` through the admin API; no env var configures them. The agent does not emit or wire OpenTelemetry. Operators who want OTel metrics can enable Claude Code's own OpenTelemetry export on the operator side as an optional alternative. See [observability.md](observability.md) for error reporting.

### Slack

Slack vars are env-var-only (secrets); the agent does not function as a Slack bot without them.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | `string` | required for Slack | Slack bot user OAuth token (`xoxb-...`). |
| `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` | `string` | required for Slack | Slack app-level token for Socket Mode (`xapp-...`). Settable via the admin UI agent detail page's "Connect Slack" action or as an env var. |
| `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` | `string` | required for Slack | Used to verify incoming Slack request signatures. |
| `SLACK_ADMIN_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Optional admin-level token for privileged Slack operations. |
| `SLACK_ALERT_CHANNEL` | `string` | — | Slack channel ID to post system alerts (e.g. startup errors, trial-expiry warnings). |
| `SLACK_OWNER_USER` | `string` | — | Slack user ID of the agent owner, used for DM fallback. |
| `SLACK_CHANNEL_ID` | `string` | — | Slack channel for the current run. Not user-configured: injected per run by the runtime (`runtime/spawn-env.ts`, `runtime/cron-handler.ts`). Slack-triggered runs get it set; cron runs also get it (the configured alert/report channel) but no `SLACK_THREAD_TS`. |
| `SLACK_THREAD_TS` | `string` | — | Slack thread timestamp to reply into for the current run. Not user-configured: injected per run for Slack-triggered runs only (DMs and @mentions). Cron runs never get it because they have no originating thread. |

### GitHub

Provide either the GitHub App vars (recommended) or `GH_TOKEN` (PAT). App auth is used when the App env vars are present; `GH_TOKEN` is the fallback. For multi-org installs see [github-multi-org.md](github-multi-org.md).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GH_APP_ID` | `string` | required for App auth | GitHub App ID (integer as string). With `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, enables App auth; `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` is an optional pin. Settable via the admin UI agent detail page's "Set up GitHub App" action or as an env var. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` | `string` | — (optional pin) | Optional pin: an installation ID that is always used (and is the default `gh-token` installation) even before repo scope syncs. Without it, the agent discovers the App's installations and uses those whose owner is in the agent's repo scope; App auth engages only if the pin is set or at least one usable installation is found, otherwise the `GH_TOKEN` PAT path (if set) runs and discovery retries each config-sync tick. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | `string` | required for App auth | PEM private key for the GitHub App (newlines may be `\n`-escaped). Required with `GH_APP_ID`. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID` | `string` | — | OAuth client ID for the GitHub App, persisted from the manifest-flow exchange so the App's OAuth settings can be reconfigured later without redoing the flow. Env-var-only (not secret). |
| `GH_APP_CLIENT_SECRET` | `string` | — | OAuth client secret for the GitHub App, persisted from the manifest-flow exchange. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `GH_APP_SLUG` | `string` | — | URL slug of the agent's GitHub App, persisted from the manifest-flow exchange so the install link (`https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new`) can be rebuilt later. Env-var-only (not secret). |
| `GH_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Personal Access Token. Settable via the admin UI agent detail page's "Add GitHub PAT" action or as an env var. Used only when GitHub App vars are absent. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER` | `string` | — | Owner hint under GitHub App auth: names the org whose `gh-token.d/<owner>` token the `gh` wrapper (`scripts/bin/gh`) and git credential helper use. Set per spawn by `runtime/spawn-env.ts` and per call by the `gh` helpers in `runtime/gh-helpers.ts`. Unset fails with a teaching error; an owner with no token file fails naming the org. Ignored under PAT auth. |

### Platform

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SHIPWRIGHT_API_URL` | `string` | — | Base URL of the admin service, used by the runtime entrypoint to fetch config at startup. Also settable via `--api-url`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ID` | `string` | — | The agent's ID on the platform. Also settable via `--agent-id`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_TYPE` | `string` | — | The agent's Specialty name. Set by the entrypoint from `specialty` on `GET /agents/:id/config` (pre-AGR-6.3 runtime images read the deprecated `typeName` alias, which the response still carries) before it spawns the agent server; `ensureAgentHome()` (`runtime/setup.ts`) uses it to pick the workspace template directory from the type manifest. Unset or unresolvable types fall back to the default specialty. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_REPO_ROOT` | `string` | three levels above `runtime/` | Repo root the runtime uses to register the built-in `shipwright` marketplace (`installPlugins()`) and to find `specialties/` (`resolveTemplatesDir()`), both in `runtime/setup.ts`. In the platform image layout (`/app/runtime`) the computed default resolves to `/`, so derived images set this to the directory holding `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Unset or empty keeps the computed default. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_SPECIALTIES_DIR` | `string` | repo-root `specialties/` | Directory holding `<type>/manifest.yaml` specialty manifests. Read by the admin specialty manifest loader (`admin/src/specialty-manifest-loader.ts`) and by the runtime's workspace-template lookup (`runtime/setup.ts`). See [specialties.md](specialties.md). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE` | `string` | `coding` | Universal fallback specialty: the admin registry resolves unknown types to this manifest, and the runtime uses it when no type is set. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_AGENT_TYPE` | `string` | `SHIPWRIGHT_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE` | Specialty stamped on agents that account users create via self-serve, in both the admin UI and the JSON API (`admin/src/account-agent-create.ts`). See [self-serve.md](self-serve.md). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_API_KEY` | `string` | — | Bearer token for the config fetch at startup (`/agents/:id/config` and `/agents/:id/crons`). Also settable via `--api-key`. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_PR_STATE_RECONCILER_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `2700000` (45 min) | Interval in milliseconds of the runtime's periodic-pass tick (`runtime/boot.ts`, Step 5b). Each tick runs the runtime's own passes first (currently `worktree-reaper`), then any passes the loaded extension contributes; each pass has its own error handling so one failure does not block the others. Deliberately longer than the 60s config and cron syncs. Only started when the runtime has an admin client and `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ID` is configured. |

### Server

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `number` | `3000` | Hono server port for the admin service (`admin/src/admin-boot.ts`). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_HEALTH_PORT` | `number` | `3459` | Dedicated health server port for K8s liveness probes. Bound by the agent server process (`runtime/boot.ts`), which owns the single health server. |
| `NODE_ENV` | `string` | — | Runtime environment. Set to `production` to enforce production-safety guards (blocks `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH`). |
| `SENTRY_DSN` | `string` | — | Sentry error reporting DSN, read independently by the agent runtime and the admin service. When set, each initializes Sentry (`lib/sentry.ts`), reports unhandled errors, and mounts error-capture middleware on 5xx. When unset, Sentry is fully inert (no init call, zero telemetry). It must be present at process startup: init is evaluated once at module load, before the 60-second config sync, so delivering it through the agent config bundle instead of the pod env leaves Sentry inactive for the pod's lifetime. Agents are provisioned per tenant by `KubernetesAgentProvisioner`, so operators set it directly in the agent's own env, the same way as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Env-var-only (secret). See [observability.md](observability.md). |
| `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` | `string` | — | Sentry environment tag. Defaults to `NODE_ENV` if unset, then `production`. Optional alongside `SENTRY_DSN`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `60000` (60 sec) | Tick cadence in milliseconds for the trial-expiry sweeper (`admin/src/trial-expiry-sweeper.ts`), a background job in the admin service that disables all enabled AgentCronJob records of agents whose `trialExpiresAt` has passed. Each tick finds every cron belonging to an expired-trial agent and sets it `enabled:false` via `AgentCronJobService.setEnabled()`, the same method the `PATCH /agents/:id/crons/:cronId` route uses. It deliberately does **not** deprovision the agent (no workload teardown, no token revocation), since a customer may convert to paid later. Idempotent. Blank, non-numeric, zero and negative values fall back to the default. |

### Admin and chat services

For comprehensive documentation of the chat service architecture, authentication, data model, queue behavior and API endpoints, see [chat-service.md](chat-service.md).

The platform feature flags (`SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_CRON_RUN_NOW_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_TOKEN_MINT_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_DOC_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_TRANSCRIPT_API_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_REPO_ACCESS_CHECK_ENABLED`, `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ENABLED`) all default to off and follow one convention: the feature is on only when the value is the literal string `enabled`. `true`, `1`, `on` and any other value leave it off. This table is maintained by hand; `bun run check:config-docs` (`scripts/check-config-docs.ts`) scans every `process.env.*` reference under `runtime/`, `admin/` and `chat/` and fails when a variable is missing from it.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN` | `string` | required | Postgres connection string for the admin service schema (e.g. `postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db`). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_API_KEYS` | `string` | — | Admin service only. Comma-separated `name:token:scope` tuples for bearer token auth. Scope is `*`, an agent id, `platform.read` or `platform.ops` (no colons in scopes). See [agent-api.md](agent-api.md). Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. Self-serve signup is on only when this is exactly `enabled`. Companion vars `SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS`, `_CONTACT_EMAIL` and `_AGENT_TYPE` are covered in [admin-service.md](admin-service.md). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. The agent-to-agent ask routes (`POST /agents/{id}/ask`, `GET /agents/{id}/asks`) are on only when this is exactly `enabled`; otherwise they return 404. See [agent-api-resources.md](agent-api-resources.md). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CRON_RUN_NOW_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. The cron run-now route (`POST /agents/{id}/crons/{cronId}/run-now`) is on only when this is exactly `enabled`; otherwise it returns 404. See [agent-api-ops.md](agent-api-ops.md#cron-run-now). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST` | `string` | — | Admin service only. Comma-separated directional `from>to` agent-id pairs allowed to ask (e.g. `agent-a>agent-b,agent-b>agent-c`). Empty or unset denies every pair (403). A malformed pair makes the admin service throw at boot, naming the pair. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_TRANSCRIPT_API_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. The cron-run transcript routes (`PUT`/`GET /agents/{id}/crons/{cronId}/runs/{runId}/transcript`) are on only when this is exactly `enabled`; otherwise they return 404. When on, the config bundle's `features.transcriptUpload` is true and the runtime uploads a redacted transcript after each cron run. See [agent-api-resources.md](agent-api-resources.md#transcripts). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_REPO_ACCESS_CHECK_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. When exactly `enabled`, the config bundle's `features.repoAccessCheck` is true and the runtime probes each scoped repo's read/write access (once per 30-minute installations heartbeat and on repo-scope change), reporting it as `repos` on `PUT /agents/{id}/github-installations`. Otherwise the runtime makes no probe calls. See [agent-api-resources.md](agent-api-resources.md#github-installations-snapshot). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. Provisioned agent pods run as the Agent row's `podServiceAccountName` only when this is exactly `enabled`; otherwise the column is never rendered into the Deployment, even if set. Cannot be combined with Anthropic federation for the same agent (the manifest build fails). Requires `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_PROVISIONING=enabled`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_TOKEN_MINT_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. The chat-credential routes (`POST`/`GET /agents/{id}/chat-credentials`, `DELETE /agents/{id}/chat-credentials/{tokenId}`) are on only when this is exactly `enabled`; otherwise they return 404. See [agent-api-resources.md](agent-api-resources.md). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_DOC_ENABLED` | `string` | — | Admin service only. `GET /doc` (the platform OpenAPI 3.1 document, behind the admin auth middleware) is mounted only when this is exactly `enabled`; otherwise the route is absent (404). See [agent-api-resources.md](agent-api-resources.md). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_POOL_HOLD_THRESHOLD_MS` | `number` | `2000` | Admin service only. A pg pool connection held longer than this many milliseconds before release is logged (`pg connection held past threshold`) with the request route, hold duration and pool stats. Non-positive or non-numeric values fall back to the default. Observability only. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_POOL_MONITOR_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `30000` | Admin service only. Interval for the pool monitor, which logs the pool snapshot (`pg pool has waiting clients`) only while clients are queued. Stopped on graceful shutdown. Non-positive or non-numeric values fall back to the default. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL` | `string` | — | Base URL of the chat service (e.g. `http://chat:3000`). When set alongside `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_TOKEN`, the agent starts the chat poll loop (`runtime/boot.ts`, Step 6b) to poll for pending messages and reply. The admin service reads it too, for the chat UI and token minting. Optional; omit to disable chat. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Bearer token for the agent to call the chat service. Required alongside `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL` to enable the chat poll loop. Tokens are scoped to their agent ID. Env-var-only (secret). When `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_PROVISIONING=enabled`, the admin provisioner mints it per agent, stores it in the agent Secret (key `chat-service-token`) and injects it into the agent Deployment under this name. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `5000` | Poll interval in milliseconds for the chat poll loop. The agent claims one unclaimed message per thread per poll cycle and runs it through Claude. Only used when the chat URL and token are configured. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_ADMIN_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Bearer token for admin-side chat-service token minting. Required (alongside `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL`) to enable per-agent provisioning at agent-creation time and full agent deletion via `DELETE /agents/:id`. The admin service uses it to call the chat service's `POST /tokens` and `DELETE /tokens/:id` (mint on provision, revoke on delete). Env-var-only (secret). |
| `DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT` | `string` | required | Chat service only. Postgres connection string for the dedicated chat database (never shared with the admin database). The chat service applies `prisma migrate deploy` against it at boot; the chat integration suites skip when it is unset. |
| `CHAT_SEED_ADMIN_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Chat service only. When set, the chat service upserts it as an admin token at boot. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `CHAT_STALLED_AFTER_MS` | `number` | `300000` | Chat service only. Age in milliseconds after which a claimed message with no reply is marked stalled by the stall reaper. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_AGENTS_URL` | `string` | — | Chat service only. Base URL of the admin service used to resolve token scopes. The scope resolver is enabled only when this and `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_AGENTS_API_KEY` are both set. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_AGENTS_API_KEY` | `string` | — | Chat service only. Bearer credential for the scope-resolver calls to `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_AGENTS_URL`. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_PUSH_WEBHOOK_URL` | `string` | — | Chat service only. Admin webhook URL notified when an agent reply lands. The reply notifier is enabled only when this and `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` are both set. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Chat service only. Dedicated bearer credential for the reply webhook (never reuses the agents API key); set to the same value as the admin side's `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_SECRET` | `string` | — | HS256 secret for the `admin_session` cookie. The admin service signs it on login; any other service verifying that session must share the value. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | `string` | — | 64-char hex (32 bytes) for AES-256-GCM encryption of secrets at rest. **If unset, secrets are stored in plain text.** Always set it in any real deployment. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_ALLOWED_EMAILS` | `string` | — | Comma-separated list of email addresses permitted to log in to the admin UI via either Google OAuth or Okta OIDC. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_APP_BASE_URL` | `string` | `http://localhost:{PORT}` | Public base URL of the admin service, used to build the OAuth/OIDC redirect URIs for both Google and Okta. An explicit value always wins. When deployed via Helm with `networking.type=ingress` or `gateway`, the chart auto-derives it from the ingress/gateway host when empty; for other install types the env var stays omitted unless set explicitly. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUBLIC_REPO` | `string` | — | Repository slug (`org/repo`) scoped for the public read-only task board. When set, `GET /public/tasks` shows tasks for this repo only, unauthenticated. When unset, the board renders in degraded mode (empty table plus warning). Optional. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TZ` | `string` | `America/Los_Angeles` | IANA timezone name (e.g. `America/New_York`) for date/time display in the admin UI. Validated at startup: an invalid value logs an error and exits. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` | `string` | — | VAPID public key (base64url, uncompressed P-256 point) for Web Push notifications on agent replies. Sent to the browser (NOT a secret). Web Push is enabled only when public + private + subject are ALL set; otherwise the push routes 503, the chat page renders no toggle, and the app degrades to the poll-only experience. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` | `string` | — | VAPID private key (base64url raw P-256 scalar) used to sign the RFC 8292 VAPID JWT. Env-var-only (secret; masked in admin env responses and scrubbed by Sentry). Required alongside the public key and subject to enable Web Push. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_SUBJECT` | `string` | — | VAPID `sub` claim: a `mailto:` address or an https URL identifying the push sender per RFC 8292. Required alongside the public and private keys to enable Web Push. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_MAX_DETAIL` | `generic` \| `title` \| `preview` | `title` | Operator hard ceiling for how much detail a push notification may reveal on a locked screen. `generic` = "Your agent replied" only; `title` = + thread title; `preview` = + up to 120 chars. The effective per-notification level is `min(this ceiling, the subscription's own opt-in)`. Agent names, ids, repo names, file paths and costs are never included at any level. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_SESSION_ALERT_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `60000` | Tick cadence (ms) of the session-alert sweeper, the background loop that sends "session is waiting" / daily-reminder / "session completed" push notifications to session followers. It only starts when Web Push is fully configured (all three VAPID vars) and the task-store integration is configured on the admin service; otherwise it is never registered. Blank, non-numeric, zero and negative values fall back to the default. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | `string` | — | Shared bearer token the chat service presents to the admin `POST /admin/push/notify` webhook to trigger a "your agent replied" notification. Env-var-only (secret). Required (alongside a full VAPID config) for the inbound reply trigger. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS` | `number` | `3` | How many days before `trialExpiresAt` the trial-expiry warning sweeper (`admin/src/trial-expiry-warning-sweeper.ts`) sends its one Slack alert to an agent's own `SLACK_ALERT_CHANNEL`. The sweeper always runs, ticks hourly, finds agents with `trialExpiresAt` set and `trialExpiryWarnedAt` still null, and stamps `trialExpiryWarnedAt` after a successful send so an agent is never warned twice. The firing band is symmetric: a trial that already lapsed is still warned once, but only up to the same number of days past `trialExpiresAt`; older ones are counted as `stale` and never alerted, so enabling this on a fleet with long-lapsed trials cannot cause a retroactive alert burst. Blank, non-numeric, zero and negative values fall back to the default. |
| `METRICS_DASHBOARD_URL` | `string` | `/dashboard` | URL for the "Metrics" toolbar link in the admin UI. The default is a same-host relative path, suitable when the ingress routes `/dashboard` to a metrics service on the same hostname. Set an absolute URL when the metrics service runs on a different host or port. |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `string` | — | Google OAuth 2.0 client ID. Required for the admin UI login flow. The login page shows "Sign in with Google" only when both `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are set. |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | `string` | — | Google OAuth 2.0 client secret. Required for the admin UI login flow (see `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`). Env-var-only (secret). |
| `OKTA_ISSUER` | `string` | — | Okta OIDC issuer URL (e.g. `https://your-org.okta.com/oauth2/default`). Required to enable the admin UI's `/admin/auth/okta` login flow; when unset, those routes redirect to the login page with `error=server_error` and Google login is unaffected. The login page shows only the configured providers; with neither configured it shows a misconfiguration notice and no buttons. |
| `OKTA_CLIENT_ID` | `string` | — | Okta OIDC client ID. Required for the admin UI Okta login flow. |
| `OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET` | `string` | — | Okta OIDC client secret. Required for the admin UI Okta login flow. Env-var-only (secret). |

### Agent provisioning (admin service)

Controls how the admin service provisions the Kubernetes workload backing each agent at creation time and tears it down as part of `DELETE /agents/:id`. When provisioning is disabled (the default), create/delete only write the database row and trigger optional external cleanup (chat-service token revocation) if their URLs and tokens are configured. No cluster is required. See the [shipwright Kubernetes provisioning guide](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/deploy-kubernetes-provisioning.md) for the chart side.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_PROVISIONING` | `string` | — | Set to `enabled` to provision a real Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim + Secret + Deployment per agent via `KubernetesAgentProvisioner`. Any other value (or unset) selects the no-op provisioner, preserving DB-only create/delete behavior. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_NAMESPACE` | `string` | — | Target namespace for per-agent PersistentVolumeClaim, Secret and Deployment. When unset, falls back to the downward API (the pod's own namespace). Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGE` | `string` | — | Agent container image (without tag) used for the provisioned Deployment. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGE_TAG` | `string` | `latest` | Image tag joined as `image:tag` for the provisioned Deployment. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGES` | `string` (JSON) | — | Optional per-specialty image map: a JSON object keyed by specialty whose values are `{"repository": "...", "tag": "..."}`. Provisioning, drift detection and reconcile resolve each agent's image from its specialty; an unmapped specialty (or a `default` key) falls back to `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGE`/`SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGE_TAG`. Unset or empty keeps the single image for every agent. A malformed value fails admin boot. The chart sets it from `agent.provisioning.images` when that map is non-empty. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_REPLICAS` | `number` | `1` | Replica count for the provisioned agent Deployment. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_PVC_STORAGE_GI` | `number` | `40` | Storage size in Gi for the per-agent persistent home directory (PVC). Must be large enough to hold mise caches and workspace files across pod restarts. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_PVC_NAME_TEMPLATE` | `string` | — | Template for deriving the PVC name from the agent's name. `{name}` is replaced with the agent's name (slug) when provided, or the sanitized agent ID otherwise. Example: `my-org-agent-{name}-home` gives `my-org-agent-okwow-home`. When unset, PVCs are named `{sanitizedAgentId}-home`. Useful when migrating from static agents with fixed PVC names. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_CPU_REQUEST` | `string` | `500m` | CPU request for the provisioned agent container. No CPU limit is set for platform agents, so contention throttles instead of evicting (tenant pods: see `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_CPU_LIMIT`). Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_CPU_LIMIT` | `string` | `2` | CPU limit for **tenant** agent pods only (agents with an `accountId`; those pods also carry the `shipwright.dev/tenant="true"` label on the Deployment and pod template). Platform agents never get a CPU limit. Per-account bounds come from `maxAgents` times this fixed per-pod limit (no per-account ResourceQuota, since the namespace is shared). Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_MEMORY_REQUEST` | `string` | `2Gi` | Memory request for the provisioned agent container. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_MEMORY_LIMIT` | `string` | `8Gi` | Memory limit for the provisioned agent container. Contains a runaway Claude run to its own container (OOM-kill) rather than letting it grow until the kubelet evicts neighbouring pods under node memory pressure. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_CLAUDE_POLICY_CONFIGMAP` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Name of a ConfigMap (key `managed-settings.json`) to mount read-only at `/etc/claude-code` in provisioned agent pods as Claude Code managed policy (the file lands at `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`). Empty or unset disables the mount. The chart sets it from `agent.provisioning.claudePolicy` when enabled. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_CLAUDE_POLICY_HASH` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Content hash of the policy ConfigMap, stamped on the pod template as the `shipwright.dev/claude-policy-hash` annotation so a policy change rolls agent pods. The chart sets it to the sha256 of the rendered `managed-settings.json`; because it is admin env, a policy change restarts admin, which then runs a policy-only reconcile across managed agents. Optional; ignored unless the ConfigMap name is set. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Anthropic Workload Identity Federation rule ID. When set, provisioned agent pods run as `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, mount a projected service-account token read-only at `/var/run/secrets/anthropic.com/token` (volume `anthropic-token`), and get `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` (and `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` when set) so the Anthropic client can exchange the token for a short-lived access token. Unset or empty disables federation and the other federation vars are ignored. When set, `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, `..._ORGANIZATION_ID` and `..._SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` are required; a partial config fails admin startup. The startup policy-only reconcile adds or removes this wiring on existing agents. The chart sets this and the other federation vars from `agent.provisioning.anthropicFederation` when enabled. Only read when provisioning is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Kubernetes ServiceAccount provisioned agent pods run as when federation is enabled (the projected token's subject). Required with `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`; otherwise ignored (pods keep the namespace default). The chart sets it to the agent ServiceAccount (`agent.provisioning.serviceAccount`) when federation is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_ORGANIZATION_ID` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Anthropic organization ID, injected as `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`. Required when federation is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Anthropic service account ID, injected as `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID`. Required when federation is enabled. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_WORKSPACE_ID` | `string` | _(unset)_ | Optional Anthropic workspace ID, injected as `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` only when set. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_AUDIENCE` | `string` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | Audience of the projected service-account token. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_SECONDS` | `integer` | `600` | Lifetime of the projected token (kubelet rotates it). Must be an integer >= 600 (the Kubernetes minimum); anything else fails admin startup. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_IDENTITY_MODE` | `string` | `shared` | `shared` (one identity for all agents, gated on `RULE_ID`) or `perAgent` (each agent gets its own identity; needs `ORGANIZATION_ID` and `ISSUER_ID`, does not use `RULE_ID`, `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` or `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`). Any other value fails admin startup. Federation counts as enabled in perAgent mode without a shared rule ID. In perAgent mode the admin creates each new agent's ServiceAccount, Anthropic service account and federation rule at provision time, signing in to the Admin API with its own `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` and `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID` (plus optional `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` / `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID`), which the chart renders; startup fails if any of the three is missing. See [perAgent identity mode](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/deploy-kubernetes-provisioning.md#peragent-identity-mode-opt-in). |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_ISSUER_ID` | `string` | _(unset)_ | perAgent only: Anthropic issuer ID of this cluster's OIDC issuer. Required in perAgent mode. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_NAME_SUFFIX` | `string` | _(unset)_ | perAgent only: suffix for per-agent resource names so clusters sharing an organization do not collide. Must match `^[a-z0-9-]*$`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_EPHEMERAL_STORAGE` | `string` | `4Gi` | ephemeral-storage for the provisioned agent container, applied to BOTH request and limit (kept equal, since Autopilot-style billing charges the request either way). Only read when provisioning is enabled. |

### Workspace and tooling

At startup `runtime/setup.ts` pins the mise, XDG, Go, npm and bun cache locations under `AGENT_HOME` so they land on the persistent volume. Those variables are set by the runtime, not read as overrides.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_HOME` | `string` | `/data/agent-home` | Persistent storage root. Mount a PVC here in Kubernetes so mise caches, workspace files and `~/.claude` survive pod restarts. |
| `WORKSPACE_PATH` | `string` | `$AGENT_HOME/workspace` | Explicit override for the agent workspace root (`resolveWorkspacePath()` in `runtime/workspace-paths.ts`). Resolution throws when neither this nor `AGENT_HOME` is set. |
| `MISE_DATA_DIR` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/mise` | Mise data directory, set by setup so workspace-declared runtime tools install onto the PVC. |
| `MISE_CACHE_DIR` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/mise/cache` | Mise cache directory, set by setup. |
| `XDG_CACHE_HOME` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/cache` | XDG cache directory, set by setup. |
| `GOPATH` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/go` | Go workspace root, set by setup. Go ignores `XDG_CACHE_HOME` for modules, so leaving this at its `$HOME/go` default would put the module cache on the container's ephemeral overlay, where a large dependency tree can exceed the pod's ephemeral-storage limit and evict it mid-run. |
| `GOMODCACHE` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/go/pkg/mod` | Go module cache, set by setup so it stays on the PVC. |
| `npm_config_cache` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/cache/npm` | npm cache directory, set by setup. npm does not honour `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and would otherwise write to `$HOME/.npm` on ephemeral storage. |
| `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` | `string` | `<AGENT_HOME>/cache/bun` | Bun install cache directory, set by setup. bun does not honour `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and would otherwise write to `$HOME/.bun/install/cache` on ephemeral storage. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `180000` | Maximum milliseconds the entrypoint startup sequence may take before the agent exits. Set a lower value (e.g. `10000`) in dev for faster fail-fast feedback. |
| `AGENT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` | `string` (JSON array) | — | JSON array of allowed Claude tool patterns, read by `runtime/claude.ts`. Set by the runtime's config sync from the admin service; do not set manually in production. See [agent-ops.md](agent-ops.md). |

### Voice

Optional. When unset, voice transcription and synthesis are disabled.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | `string` | — | Groq API key for voice processing. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | `string` | — | ElevenLabs API key for speech synthesis. Env-var-only (secret). |
| `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` | `string` | — | ElevenLabs voice ID to use for synthesis. |
| `PIPER_VOICE` | `string` | `en_US-hfc_female-medium` | Piper voice for local (offline) speech synthesis. Validated at startup by a discovery scan of the baked voices directory (`/app/agent/voices/`, hardcoded in `runtime/piper-voice.ts`, not env-configurable); valid values depend on what the image bakes. An unrecognized value logs loudly (naming the requested voice and every voice discovered) and falls back to the default rather than crashing. |
| `WHISPER_SERVICE_URL` | `string` | — | URL of a Whisper transcription service for voice input. |

TTS defaults to the self-hosted Piper binary baked into the agent image (no network call). `synthesizeSpeech` in `runtime/voice.ts` only calls ElevenLabs when `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` is set, and falls back to Piper otherwise. So the zero-egress voice configuration is Whisper STT with no ElevenLabs key; setting `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` or `GROQ_API_KEY` (STT) each independently reintroduces network egress to that third party. See the [shipwright voice egress matrix](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/deploy-kubernetes-addons.md#agent-voice-stttts).

**Live resolution and precedence.** Voice settings are read from live `process.env` at synthesis/transcription time (`buildVoiceConfig()` in `runtime/voice.ts`, mirroring `buildSlackAppConfig()`), not from the boot-time `config.voice` snapshot (which is kept only for Piper voice validation at startup). A per-agent `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` + `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` set via `PATCH /agents/{id}/envs` therefore takes effect on that agent within one config-sync tick (≤ 60 s) with no pod restart, while other agents keep Piper. Per-agent env wins over fleet-wide env (`admin.extraEnv`) because config-sync overwrites the process value; removing the per-agent key restores the fleet value, or Piper if there is none, on the next tick. Each `[speak:]` synthesis logs the chosen backend (`[voice] TTS backend: elevenlabs|piper`) without printing keys.

On Kubernetes these env vars are a deploy-time option of the Helm chart rather than something you set by hand. Setting `agent.voice.enabled=true` and `agent.voice.provider` (`whisper` | `groq`) makes the chart inject the matching env into provisioned agent pods. With `provider=whisper` it renders a self-hosted Whisper ASR pod and sets `WHISPER_SERVICE_URL` to its in-cluster Service. With `provider=groq` it flows `GROQ_API_KEY` from a chart-managed voice Secret. ElevenLabs TTS is opt-in and applies to both providers when set.

### Dev-only

**Do not set these in production.**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH` | `bool` | `false` | Enables `GET /admin/dev-login` (bypasses OAuth/OIDC provider login, mints a dev session). Blocked when `NODE_ENV=production` (`admin/src/dev-auth-guard.ts`). |
